title: Dynamic Memory and Host Capacity in Plain English
summary: Understand why Hyper-V memory settings must balance guest demand, restart reliability and host capacity rather than simply maximizing consolidation.
plain_language_explanation: Dynamic Memory lets Hyper-V adjust assigned memory within configured limits. Startup, minimum and maximum memory serve different purposes, while Smart Paging is a temporary restart aid under specific memory-pressure conditions rather than a normal performance mechanism.
quick_check: Why is setting a very low minimum memory not automatically a good consolidation strategy?

title: Hyper-V Storage Architecture, VHDX and Production Capacity Design
summary: Design VM storage using supported Hyper-V storage architectures, virtual-disk formats and capacity controls with clear performance and resiliency trade-offs.
objective: Compare local, SAN/NAS and software-defined storage patterns and relate fixed, dynamic and differencing virtual disks to operational risk, performance and capacity management.
body_outline: Hyper-V supports standalone local storage as well as clustered SAN, NAS and software-defined storage architectures; availability assumptions differ between them.
VHDX is the modern virtual-disk format and fixed, dynamic and differencing allocation models have distinct capacity and performance characteristics.
Storage QoS can apply minimum/maximum IOPS controls and provides a mechanism for performance isolation and monitoring.
Disk expansion, optimization, checkpoint growth and free-space headroom must be governed as lifecycle operations rather than ad-hoc fixes.
quick_check: Which evidence should be collected before approving a VHDX resize or storage migration for a production VM?

title: Dynamic Memory, Smart Paging, vNUMA and Processor Compatibility
summary: Relate Hyper-V memory and processor controls to NUMA locality, restart behavior, workload performance and migration compatibility.
architecture_notes: Dynamic Memory changes the amount of memory presented to a running VM within policy limits. Smart Paging is intentionally constrained to specific restart scenarios. VM configuration version controls feature availability, and processor compatibility can trade exposed CPU capabilities for migration compatibility; Windows Server 2025 adds dynamic processor compatibility for eligible clustered VMs.
failure_modes: startup RAM below guest installation or upgrade requirements
host memory pressure causing restart or consolidation risk
persistent reliance on paging masking undersized capacity
oversized VMs crossing NUMA boundaries without workload justification
processor compatibility enabled without understanding workload performance impact
configuration-version upgrade performed before mixed-host compatibility is confirmed
enterprise_design_notes: Baseline workload demand and host reserve, document NUMA/CPU topology, validate migration requirements, and treat configuration-version upgrades as one-way compatibility decisions that require estate readiness.

title: Read-Only Hyper-V Capacity, Storage and Network Evidence Pack
summary: Collect host and VM evidence for memory, processors, virtual disks, switches, VLANs and migration readiness without changing production state.
objective: Build a timestamped evidence pack suitable for capacity, migration and incident review before any change is approved.
steps: Record VM startup/minimum/maximum memory, assigned memory and dynamic-memory state.
Record virtual processor count, NUMA exposure and processor compatibility state where available.
List VM virtual disks, paths and current size metadata; record host/storage free-space separately.
List Hyper-V virtual switches, VM adapters and VLAN configuration.
Record live-migration configuration and relevant host versions without initiating a migration.
Correlate findings with workload symptoms and change history before proposing remediation.
expected_result: A read-only capacity, storage and network evidence pack with no VM, switch, VLAN, disk or migration changes.

title: Hyper-V Storage, Memory or Network Performance Incident: Evidence-First Decision Tree
summary: Diagnose production performance degradation by separating guest demand, host contention, storage latency/capacity and virtual-network causes before changing configuration.
diagnostic_order: Define the symptom, affected VMs, start time and recent changes before tuning anything.
Compare guest memory demand with assigned memory, host pressure and restart history.
Check virtual-disk location, free-space headroom, latency/IOPS evidence and checkpoint state.
Map VM adapters to switches/VLANs and compare affected versus healthy paths.
Check processor/NUMA and migration-compatibility context where symptoms correlate with placement or host changes.
Escalate with preserved evidence when remediation requires disk operations, switch/VLAN changes, VM shutdown or processor-compatibility changes.
escalation_boundary: Do not resize/optimize disks, alter memory/CPU settings, change VLANs or virtual switches, enable processor compatibility, or migrate production VMs as part of diagnosis without approved change and recovery controls.

title: Hyper-V Virtual Networking, VLANs and Mobility Design
summary: Design Hyper-V virtual networking and migration paths using explicit switch, VLAN, bandwidth and compatibility evidence.
objective: Explain virtual-switch policy, VLAN tagging, network isolation and processor/network prerequisites that influence reliable VM placement and migration.
body_outline: Hyper-V Virtual Switch is a software-based Layer-2 switch with connectivity, isolation, policy and diagnostic capabilities.
VLAN configuration depends on coordinated physical-switch, host-switch and VM-adapter settings; trunk scenarios require deliberate design rather than duplicate tagging.
Bandwidth controls and hardware offload capabilities must be validated against the physical NIC, driver, switch and workload requirements rather than assumed.

Live-migration reliability depends on host compatibility, authentication, storage accessibility and sufficient network capacity; processor compatibility can solve only specific same-manufacturer CPU feature mismatches.
quick_check: A VM loses connectivity only after migration to one host. Which switch, VLAN and physical-network evidence should be compared before changing the VM?

title: Hyper-V Production Operations Assessment
summary: Scenario assessment covering storage architecture, Dynamic Memory, processor compatibility, virtual networking and evidence-led capacity decisions.

assessment_items.question: Why should Smart Paging not be treated as normal memory capacity?
assessment_items.answer: It is a temporary restart mechanism used only under specific memory-pressure conditions and can reduce performance because disk is much slower than RAM.

assessment_items.question: What is the risk of upgrading a VM configuration version before all intended hosts are ready?
assessment_items.answer: The VM might no longer start on hosts that do not support the newer configuration version, so mixed-host compatibility must be checked first.

assessment_items.question: A storage-heavy VM is affecting neighbors. What should be proven before applying QoS or moving it?
assessment_items.answer: Measure workload demand, latency/IOPS, disk path and host/storage contention, then validate the proposed QoS or placement target against the actual bottleneck.

assessment_items.question: Why can identical VM VLAN settings still produce different connectivity after migration?
assessment_items.answer: The destination host can differ in virtual-switch mapping, management/physical adapter configuration, upstream trunk allowance, driver/firmware or network path state.

title: Senior Hyper-V Interview: Storage, Capacity and Network Operations
summary: Senior production scenarios testing capacity reasoning, safe storage operations, Dynamic Memory, VLAN diagnosis and migration compatibility.

questions.question: A host is memory-constrained and several VMs restart slowly. What do you inspect before increasing or reducing VM memory?
answer_points: guest OS and application memory requirements
capacity remediation options before configuration changes

questions.question: A production VHDX is almost full at the storage layer. What is your safe decision sequence?
answer_points: confirm datastore/volume free space and growth trend
separate guest filesystem capacity from VHDX/container capacity
choose supported resize/storage action under change control

questions.question: A live migration fails only between two CPU generations. What does processor compatibility solve and what does it not solve?
answer_points: compare exact CPU manufacturer and feature sets
understand standard versus Windows Server 2025 dynamic compatibility
recognize compatibility mode hides some CPU features
it does not enable migration between different CPU manufacturers
test workload performance and rollback constraints

questions.question: After host maintenance, one VM has no network despite being healthy. What do you compare first?
answer_points: healthy VM/host comparison and event evidence
